coaching.headline: We won the early scraps, took fuck all from them, then fed Drongo and Sevarog kills for the rest of the night.
coaching.team: We won two early fights and turned neither into a structure, then lost nine structures while taking four. Sevarog got fat off our offlane, the one Fangtooth we took was followed by two of our towers falling, and the third Fangtooth went to them with nobody on our side dead. We placed more wards than they did, but they cleared ten of ours and we cleared one. That is a team that let a free Fangtooth go and left their vision standing.
coaching.lossReflection: The cleanest alternative was early. Those two won fights were the only ones we won all game, and both ended with enemies respawning and nothing taken. Pushing the nearest wave into their outer tower, or setting up the next objective together while they were down, gives a lead something solid to stand on. It would not guarantee the rest of the game, but it beats letting the lead evaporate.

focus.title: Someone dead, nobody fights
focus.action: When one of us is dead, the other four stop picking fights and hold the wave at our nearest tower until the respawn. Whoever sees the death calls it, and nobody plays hero with a tower on the line.

34.1.call: Feng Mao was already dead and their Orb Prime was taken, and the exchange went 2-3 while our inhibitor and Core fell. With a body down and their buff secured, the job is clearing waves at the inhibitor until the respawn, not trading kills. A stalled base at least buys the next respawn.

27.3.call: Iggy & Scorch opened by killing Yurei and the exchange still went 2-3, with Drongo finishing Ikra and Feng Mao. Their inner tower and ours both fell in that window. After an opening pick, take the structure and leave before Drongo gets a clean shooting line.

18.1.call: We took their outer tower while their Mini Prime went to them in the same window, and the exchange went 2-3 with Iggy & Scorch and Grux falling first. Before the spawn, the team calls one target, Mini Prime or the tower, and commits to it together.

b501e4a5-5bdb-4389-9537-8d3b724de144.matchup: Sevarog was the lane opponent: magical ability damage, a dash that fears, a Subjugate zone that stuns anyone who leaves it, and Souls from ability kills that add health. Grux took the first kill between them, then Sevarog won the later meetings. Across the match the bigger physical threats were Skylar, their top damage dealer, plus Drongo and Yurei.
b501e4a5-5bdb-4389-9537-8d3b724de144.build: Sky Splitter's current-health on-hit and Tainted Rounds' anti-heal and low-health bonus both pay through basic attacks, and Augmentation empowers the attack after each ability cast, so the package rewards long contact with one target. Mistmeadow Buckler adds magical armor and blocks part of incoming magical damage, which fits Sevarog. Nothing in the inventory adds physical armor.
b501e4a5-5bdb-4389-9537-8d3b724de144.eternal: Thraex marks the last hero Grux basic-attacked, adding damage against that target and reducing the damage it deals to Grux. Savage Strikes adds stacking on-hit damage that heals, and Ferocity ramps attack speed the longer hero combat lasts. All of it rewards staying on one target. Golden Mane, which cuts damage from non-area hits, is a draft alternative to Ferocity if surviving the first exchange is the problem.
b501e4a5-5bdb-4389-9537-8d3b724de144.augment: Lust For Blood heals Grux for part of the damage dealt to enemies carrying maximum Bloodlust stacks. It needs a full stack of bleeds first, so it pays in long fights and does little against a quick burst. Red Mist instead grants attack speed per nearby bleeding enemy; neither changes how the first seconds of a fight go.
b501e4a5-5bdb-4389-9537-8d3b724de144.crest: Iceskorn Talons creates an ice sheet that gives allies on it physical power and movement speed and slows enemies standing on it. It is a group-fight tool that helps the team stick to a target rather than a personal escape. The match does not record when it was used.
b501e4a5-5bdb-4389-9537-8d3b724de144.improvement: Physical armor is the clearest adjustment. Skylar, Drongo and Yurei are physical and accounted for half of Grux's deaths, while the only defensive item answers magic. Tainted Rounds is not the slot to cut: it was Grux's first item and the team's earliest anti-heal item against Yurei's and Sevarog's healing, while Nerb's Tainted Scepter came last. If armor goes in, it replaces a later damage item such as Augmentation, trading some on-hit damage and haste for surviving the physical follow-up.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.matchup: The duo lane was Muriel and Ikra against Drongo and Lt. Belica. Belica's knockup and silence punish a target standing still, and Drongo's Gag Grenade silences too. Yurei was the dive threat: Severance resets on Soul Ripped targets and Soulstorm pulls them in, and Yurei took first blood on Muriel.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.build: Marshal gives nearby allies attack speed and on-hit damage, which suits Ikra's basic-attack build. Crystal Tear grants power and haste to Muriel and each hero Muriel heals or shields, and Transference returns part of an expired shield as health and adds armors while Muriel is shielded. Hexbound Bracers turns damage taken into mana and trims hero basic-attack damage. The set pays when Muriel shields often.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.eternal: Knell applies Rust on attacks and abilities, shredding both armors and giving Muriel part of what it removes. Frequency adds attack speed and haste per Rust stack, and Peal applies maximum Rust after Reversal Of Fortune. That is a shred setup on a shield support. Exarch, which empowers the basic attacks of whoever Muriel heals or shields, is the support-oriented draft alternative, trading personal shred for ally damage.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.augment: Sacrosanct drops a Consecrated Ground where Reversal Of Fortune lands, healing and speeding allies' attacks while damaging enemies and slowing theirs in that spot. It turns the global save into a fight starter. Aerial Assistance is the draft alternative if crowd control on the carry is the threat: it cleanses the ally and grants brief crowd-control immunity, trading the zone for the escape.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.crest: Silentium supplies a short silence, a Solstone and a higher ward cap, plus passive gold. The extra ward capacity suits a support who placed the most wards in the match. The silence is a tool for when Belica or Yurei commits; its uses are not recorded.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.improvement: No swap is proven necessary. If Ikra keeps getting dived, Aerial Assistance on Reversal is the most direct change. Windcaller, the common third item, gives Muriel and each shielded ally a burst of movement speed; it is lighter than Hexbound Bracers' durability, so it is worth trying only if speed rather than survival is what the duo lacks.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.matchup: Ikra and Muriel faced Drongo and Lt. Belica. Drongo's bleed and armor shred pressure from range, Belica's knockup and silence punish a carry who stands still, and Yurei could reach the backline. Ikra is a mage whose abilities deal magical damage, while Fathom basic attacks are physical.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.build: Scattershot, Terminus and Viper are physical crit and on-hit items, and Prophecy adds magical on-hit damage with attack speed. With Typhoon and Cascade this is a basic-attack Ikra. It is consistent with itself, but only Prophecy and the Typhoon crest add magical power, so Brine, Narcosis, Hydroclasm and Genesis get little extra from the build.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.eternal: Satariel grants Fearless stacks on takedowns that raise power and attack speed while lowering max health, and death removes them. Risen adds omnivamp at three or more stacks, and Psychosis raises damage to the nearest enemy hero while lowering it against everyone else. That is a snowball glass-cannon setup on Ikra; Rite is the alternative to Psychosis, trading the target restriction for haste paid in health.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.augment: Cascade builds stacks on Fathom hits to empower the next direct Brine, and ability damage grants stacking attack speed. It suits weaving abilities between basic attacks, which is what this build asks for. The Gloom, which grows bubbles and camouflages allies inside them, is the draft alternative if the duo needs protection more than damage.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.crest: Typhoon stacks attack speed on basic attacks and grants a short dash at full stacks. It supports the attack-speed plan and adds a small repositioning option against Yurei. Its activations are not recorded.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.improvement: The low damage is not proven to be the build. A fair comparison on a future Ikra game is an ability-power path built around Hydroclasm and Brine, trading on-hit consistency for burst. The field's ability core has weak results, so treat it as an experiment, not a fix.

2dfd786d-99cd-4518-8fc0-4fd9de2370c5.matchup: The mid opponent was Skylar, their top damage dealer, who killed Iggy & Scorch in both opening skirmishes, the first in their jungle. Skylar fires from Air Assault's hover and Plasma Grenade slows. Later threats were Yurei and Sevarog, who both reach a mage with no dash beyond Blink, plus Belica's silence.
2dfd786d-99cd-4518-8fc0-4fd9de2370c5.build: Orb Of Enlightenment scales with level and heals on ability casts, Dreambinder slows on ability damage, Wraith Leggings adds magical penetration and bonus damage against low-health heroes, and Oblivion Crown multiplies magical power. Tainted Scepter adds anti-heal on magical damage and stacking bonus damage. It is a coherent zone-damage build and produced our highest hero damage.
2dfd786d-99cd-4518-8fc0-4fd9de2370c5.eternal: Vesh adds a damage-over-time echo to ability damage on heroes, Mind Rot adds current-health damage to that echo, and The Tenth Seal boosts ultimate damage and haste once level ten arrives. It fits a hero who keeps enemies standing in fire. Tithe of Death, which refunds mana and grants haste on takedowns, is the alternative to The Tenth Seal if Inferno is not the main damage source.
2dfd786d-99cd-4518-8fc0-4fd9de2370c5.augment: Hold This! permanently adds explosion damage to Molotov each time it hits a hero, so it rewards landing Molotov from the start. Turret Maniac, the other common choice, trades that ramping damage for a fourth turret while every turret loses some health, which helps hold space around a tower.
2dfd786d-99cd-4518-8fc0-4fd9de2370c5.crest: Epoch puts Iggy & Scorch in stasis to wait out incoming damage, buying time for help against Yurei or Sevarog but giving no distance. Its activations are not recorded.
2dfd786d-99cd-4518-8fc0-4fd9de2370c5.improvement: Keep the damage build. If Skylar keeps winning the early skirmishes, an early defensive component against physical damage trades some slow and health for surviving Skylar's poke. Tainted Scepter's anti-heal has a target in Yurei's healing, but Muriel's passive and Grux's Tainted Rounds also cover it, so that slot is a choice rather than a must.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.matchup: Yurei was the opposing jungler: a melee diver who heals off Anima Burst, resets Severance on Soul Ripped targets and pulls with Soulstorm. Feng Mao won the head-to-head kills against Yurei. The best returns came from Belica, who has no dash beyond Blink, and Drongo, whose escapes are Blink and the in-air Shrapnel Cannon launch; most of Feng Mao's kills landed on those two.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Manta Scythe speeds clears and adds damage against isolated targets, Omen builds Momentum for an empowered attack and cooldown reduction, and The Perforator ignores part of physical armor and slows on ability damage. Draconum adds physical armor, healing amplification while dealing damage and a heal on takedown. This is the field core plus a sustain-and-armor fourth item that fits a diver taking repeated physical damage.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: Knell's Rust shreds both armors and returns some to Feng Mao, Frequency adds attack speed and haste per stack, and Peal makes attacks and abilities apply maximum Rust right after Earth Shatter. That lines the follow-up, including an Earth Shatter recast, up against shredded armor. Fracture, which adds damage against fully stacked targets, is the draft alternative to Peal for longer duels, giving up ultimate haste.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.augment: Ichorous Glaive restores missing health on kills, much more on Earth Shatter executions. It rewards the reset style that produced eleven kills, but it only heals after the kill and does not protect the seconds that follow if Drongo is still shooting. Imperial Duelist is the steadier alternative, trading kill healing for more damage and less damage taken against the target Feng Mao is attacking.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.crest: Ortus grants movement speed and physical power on activation, and takedowns inside the window permanently add power and refresh it. It suits a jungler chasing resets. Its activations are not recorded.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.improvement: No item swap is proven. The repeated pattern was dying right after a kill, which is a decision, not an inventory problem. If Drongo keeps finishing Feng Mao, a second armor item over a damage slot trades kill pressure for surviving the follow-up.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Support job done where it counts: a hand in 65% of our kills, the most wards on the map, and Ikra never died before the ten-minute mark. That is the standard.

Muriel died first in two early skirmishes: first blood to Yurei, then to Drongo deep in their jungle beside Feng Mao. Before following an early invade, Muriel waits until Yurei is visible; dead supports shield nobody.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Lowest hero damage of our four damage dealers, so Ikra's output is the gap to close. Only three deaths is a decent base; now Willy Guggenheim needs the damage to come with it.
Yurei is their backline diver. When Yurei drops off the map, Willy Guggenheim keeps Narcosis for the dash instead of poke; the suspend is what lets Muriel and Grux turn on the diver.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Eleven kills and our highest objective damage. Xeebs was the one actually stabbing people, mostly Belica and Drongo, and that target choice is right.

Three times Feng Mao landed a kill and died seconds later, twice to Drongo. Finishing and then sticking around for the cuddle gets a jungler fucked. After the kill, find Drongo; if Drongo is alive and shooting, leave.
Feng Mao cleared no enemy wards again while they cleared ten of ours. Next game Xeebs calls the Fangtooth plan before each spawn and checks the pit entrances for their vision before the team commits.
b501e4a5-5bdb-4389-9537-8d3b724de144: Grux died to Sevarog five times, and every kill Sevarog lands with an ability adds Souls. After the second loss to Sevarog, hold the wave under tower and call Xeebs before trading again. Good damage, wasted by dying.

Mistmeadow Buckler handles Sevarog's magic, but Skylar, Drongo and Yurei took the other five and nothing in the build stops physical damage. Against three physical threats, physical armor goes in by the third item.
2dfd786d-99cd-4518-8fc0-4fd9de2370c5: Top hero damage on the team, so the fire was landing. The early skirmishes were not: Skylar killed Iggy & Scorch in both opening skirmishes. Iggy & Scorch sets turrets and oil before following an invade into Skylar.
The last two deaths went to Yurei. Epoch is built for that exact moment: when Yurei or Sevarog commits onto Iggy & Scorch, stasis buys the team time to turn on the diver.

threats: Chain-CC risk (1 hard-CC abilities, ~0.5s of lockdown): Lt. Belica Neural Disruptor (silence 0.5s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Dive threat on our backline: Yurei. Assign peel for the carry and ward the flanks.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Grux Crush (knockup 0.5s), Iggy & Scorch Inferno (knockback). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Muriel) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Smash 'n Grab pull → Crush knockup → Warlord's Challenge stun → bleed-stacked basics
ourKits.winCondition: land the pull→knockup chain to lock a target while bleed and AS shred them
ourKits.passive: basics stack a bleed for sustained damage
ourKits.playWith: follow-up burst inside his knockup/stun window
ourKits.playAgainst: telegraphed engage — bait Crush/Pull, then punish; kite his slow start

ourKits.combo: Alacrity shield+AS → Consecrated Ground bubble → Reversal global save
ourKits.winCondition: keep the carry alive with global shields and enable their damage
ourKits.passive: abilities grant Sentinel to allies; on-hit bonus
ourKits.playAgainst: she has no damage threat — dive her carry through the shields or pick her first

ourKits.combo: Oil Spill → Molotov ignite → Flame Turret → Inferno knockback ult
ourKits.winCondition: layer fire zones on a choke/objective and burn the team
ourKits.playWith: CC that holds enemies in his fire
ourKits.playAgainst: don't fight in his zones — flank; kill the turret, dive him

ourKits.combo: Reaping Dash → Hamstring slows → Safeguard spellshield → Earth Shatter execute
ourKits.winCondition: trade with the spellshield up and execute low targets with Earth Shatter
ourKits.passive: permanent power on unique hero takedowns
ourKits.playWith: setup that holds a target for the execute
ourKits.playAgainst: bait Safeguard's spellshield before committing the key CC

enemyKits.combo: Plasma Grenade → Hypercharge on-hit → Air Assault reposition → Atomiser ult
enemyKits.winCondition: Hypercharge and kite-shoot from Air Assault safety
enemyKits.passive: extra jump; kills cause corpse explosions
enemyKits.playWith: a frontline so she can free-fire airborne
enemyKits.playAgainst: CC her out of Air Assault; she's squishy on the ground

enemyKits.combo: Old Rusty slow → Gag Grenade silence → Rad Rounds basics → Shrapnel Cannon armor shred
enemyKits.winCondition: kite back, stack Wastelander bleed and Rad Rounds, melt from range
enemyKits.playWith: peel and frontline so he can free-fire
enemyKits.playAgainst: low mobility — dive him or break LoS through his poke; he folds to hard engage

enemyKits.combo: Anima Burst / Whispering Echoes apply Soul Rip → Severance resets on Soul-Ripped targets → Soulstorm pulls them in
enemyKits.winCondition: chain Severance resets to stick to a target and burst in melee
enemyKits.passive: casting grants ranged empowered basics + attack speed
enemyKits.playWith: follow-up CC to hold the target she dashes onto
enemyKits.playAgainst: her chain needs Soul Rip resets — peel/disengage breaks it; punish when Severance is on cooldown

enemyKits.combo: Phantom Rush → Subjugate root → Siphon → Colossal Blow
enemyKits.winCondition: stack Souls to snowball Siphon and lock down with the root
enemyKits.passive: ability kills grant permanent Soul stacks (HP + damage)
enemyKits.playWith: a team that converts his root into kills
enemyKits.playAgainst: deny his last-hits early to starve Souls; dodge the slow Subjugate

enemyKits.combo: Seismic Assault knockup → Void Bomb → Neural Disruptor silence ult, Void Drone mana drain
enemyKits.winCondition: knock up + silence a target and burst with missing-HP scaling
enemyKits.playAgainst: dodge Seismic Assault; she's immobile — dive when ult is down
